title: Running on empty
hook: Tired, stretched thin, or low for a while? That's worth taking seriously, and getting help is part of faith.

screens.text: Becoming Muslim changes a lot at once: new habits, new people, maybe tension at home or lost friends. Six weeks in, plenty of people feel worn out. Today is about stress, burnout and your mental health, and how to get help.

**You're carrying a lot.** Converts often juggle learning a faith, family stress and loneliness all at once [Research Notes - Retention and Convert Voices]. Your faith isn't measured by how exhausted you are.
bubbles: Allah knows your limits: *"Allāh does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity"* [Q 2:286, Saheeh Intl.].

screens.prompt: How burnout happens, and how it passes

points.label: All in
points.text: Some converts try everything at once: every extra prayer, extra fasts, three classes, no sleep.

points.label: The crash
points.text: Then they crash [Field Guide ch. 9]. The Prophet ﷺ warned that whoever overloads himself in the religion will be overcome by it [Bukhari 39].

points.label: Rest
points.text: He told a Companion who prayed all night and fasted every day to stop: your body has a right over you [Bukhari 1975].

points.label: Steady
points.text: Keep the five prayers, let the extras rest for now, sleep, and tell someone. Regular and sustainable beats intense and short-lived.

screens.situation: Dre is six weeks in. He prays every extra prayer, fasts Mondays and Thursdays, takes two online classes, and sleeps five hours. Lately he dreads all of it and snapped at his mom.

options.text: Keep the five prayers, drop the extras for now, sleep more, and tell his mentor how he's feeling
options.feedback: Yes. The five stay; the extras can wait. Regular and sustainable beats intense and short-lived [Bukhari 39].

options.text: Push harder, since feeling tired means his iman is weak
options.feedback: Not quite. Exhaustion isn't weak faith. The Prophet ﷺ told people to rest [Bukhari 1975].

options.text: Quit everything, including prayer, until he feels better
options.feedback: Not quite. The five prayers stay. Cut the extras, not the core.

screens.text: **Sadness isn't weak faith.** When his baby son died, the Prophet ﷺ cried. Asked about it, he said this was mercy: the eyes shed tears and the heart grieves [Bukhari 1303].
bubbles: The prophet Ya'qub (Jacob) grieved for years and said, *"I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allāh"* [Q 12:86, Saheeh Intl.].
Feeling low doesn't mean you're doing Islam wrong.

screens.prompt: Mental health and faith: true or myth?

items.text: "If I prayed more, I wouldn't feel this way."
items.why: Myth. Prayer and remembrance do calm the heart [Q 13:28]. Depression and anxiety are also real health conditions. You can need both.

items.text: "Seeing a therapist means my faith is weak."
items.why: Myth. Allah created a treatment for every illness [Bukhari 5678]. Getting help is taking the means, like tying your camel.
Myth. Your body has a right over you [Bukhari 1975]. Sleep, food and a walk care for the trust Allah gave you.
Myth. Telling someone is often the first step to feeling better. You don't have to carry it alone.

items.text: "Remembering Allah can bring my heart rest."
items.why: True. Hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah [Q 13:28], alongside any other help you need.

screens.text: **Therapy and faith go together.** A good counselor, therapist or doctor is one of the means Allah has given you [Bukhari 5678]. Alongside that: **dhikr** (remembering Allah), du'a, and people who care about you [Q 13:28].
bubbles: You can look for a counselor who respects your faith. Ask {{mentor.name}} or {{masjid.name}} if they know one.

screens.text: Slow down. Tap once each time you say it.

**If it's more than tired.** If you're thinking about hurting yourself, or feel like you can't go on: **call or text 988** (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, US; elsewhere, your local crisis line), any time. In immediate danger, call **911**. Then tell someone you trust.
bubbles: {teen}**Under 18?** Tell a parent, a school counselor or another adult you trust. You can get help without talking about religion.{/teen}

screens.prompt: On a scale from 1 (running on empty) to 10 (full tank), where are you this week? What's one thing draining you, and one thing that refills you?

chips: I've felt low for weeks. What should I do?
How do I find a counselor who respects my faith?
I'm trying to do too much. What can I drop?
Is it okay to take medication for anxiety or depression?

screens.text: Refill your tank today, as an act of worship.
steps: Pick one: sleep an hour earlier, take a walk, eat a real meal, or call a friend
Do it with the intention of caring for the body Allah gave you
screens.optional_extra: If you've felt low for two weeks or more, tell {{mentor.name}} or a doctor this week. Saying it out loud is a strong step.

screens.text: Allah doesn't ask more than you can carry. Keep the five, drop the extras when you're worn out, and get help when you need it. Therapy and faith go together.
Rest is not quitting. Asking for help is not weakness. Slow and steady.

check.prompt: You're exhausted from doing every extra act of worship. What's the best move?

options.text: Keep the five prayers, drop the extras for now, and rest
options.feedback: Right. Whoever overloads himself in the religion gets overcome [Bukhari 39]. Steady beats intense.

options.text: Stop praying until you feel better
options.feedback: Not quite. The five stay. It's the extras you can pause.

check.prompt: Does seeing a therapist mean your faith is weak?

options.text: No. Seeking treatment is taking the means Allah provided
options.feedback: Right. Allah created a treatment for every illness [Bukhari 5678]. Faith and therapy go together.

options.text: Yes. Real faith means handling it alone
options.feedback: Not quite. The Prophet ﷺ encouraged treatment [Bukhari 5678]. Getting help is wise.

check.prompt: Someone is thinking about hurting themselves. What number can they call or text in the US, any time?

options.feedback: Right. 988 is the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline: call or text, any time. 911 for immediate danger.

options.text: There's nothing to call; just pray
options.feedback: Not quite. Pray, and also reach out: 988 by call or text, any time, and 911 in danger.

aiContext:
**Safety first (Spec §6.2 rule 6).** If the convert mentions self-harm, suicide, wanting to disappear, abuse, or any danger, stop teaching. Respond with warmth, give 988 (call or text), 911 for immediate danger, and local equivalents outside the US, and offer the consent-based alert to someone they choose. Never send a crisis only to the imam queue. Never argue, lecture or mention sin.

**Lesson facts**
- Allah doesn't burden a soul beyond its capacity [Q 2:286]. The religion is easy; whoever overburdens himself in it is overcome [Bukhari 39]. Your body has a right over you [Bukhari 1975].
- Sadness and grief aren't failures of faith: the Prophet ﷺ wept at his son's death [Bukhari 1303]; Ya'qub took his grief to Allah [Q 12:86].
- Seeking treatment is encouraged: Allah created a treatment for every disease He created [Bukhari 5678]. Remembrance of Allah brings hearts rest [Q 13:28]. Present spiritual care and professional care as partners.
- Convert context: burnout from over-zeal [Field Guide ch. 9]; practicing fully then crashing (V4); depression and loneliness (V2); converts need spiritual and counseling support, not only rules [Yaqeen 2025].

**Likely questions**
- *"I've felt low for weeks."* Validate. Suggest a doctor or counselor (two weeks or more of low mood is worth checking), the mentor, sleep and routine, and small dhikr. Keep the five prayers, gently. Watch for safety signs.
- *"How do I find a Muslim-friendly counselor?"* Ask the mentor or masjid; many therapists respect clients' faith; it's fine to ask a therapist how they handle religion. Don't name or endorse specific providers.
- *"What can I drop?"* Extra (sunnah) prayers, voluntary fasts, extra classes, ambitious Qur'an goals: pause them. Keep the five prayers and Ramadan's fast.
- *"Is medication okay?"* Seeking treatment is encouraged [Bukhari 5678]; medication questions go to their doctor; ingredient questions (e.g., alcohol in medicine) go to the imam. Never advise starting or stopping a medication.
- *"I feel like a bad Muslim because I'm depressed."* Depression isn't a sin or a sign of weak faith. Point to Bukhari 1303 and Q 12:86.

**Escalate:** any crisis (safety rule above, not the imam queue); questions about religious rulings tied to their condition (e.g., fasting with medication) to the imam; a minor in distress (encourage a trusted adult or school counselor; safeguarding rules apply).

**Don't**
- Don't diagnose, give therapy, or recommend specific medications or providers (Spec §6.2 rule 9).
- Don't say "just pray more" or imply mental illness comes from weak iman or sin.
- Don't tell anyone to drop the five prayers, even when burned out.
- Don't treat 988 as a last resort; offer it early if there's any sign of risk.
